extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Official MPEP guidance on when and how to require restriction/election among multiple inventions in a U.S. patent application, including linking claims, election of species, telephone practice, form content, and reply/traverse requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious burden standard for requiring restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must explain why there would be a serious burden on the examiner if restriction is not required. Thus the examiner must show by appropriate explanation one of the following: (A) Separate classification thereof; (B) A separate status in the art when they are classifiable together; (C) A different field of search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching legal/administrative threshold for a proper restriction requirement — the examiner must tie the burden claim to one of the enumerated bases. See accompanying enumerated bases for acceptable showings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate classification thereof
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate classification shows that each invention has attained recognition in the art as a separate subject for inventive effort, and also a separate field of search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents need not be cited to show separate classification. Use classification (class/subclass) to demonstrate separate status and field of search. If classification and field of search are the same and no clear indication of separate future classification, no reason exists for division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate status in the art when classifiable together
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though claims are classified together, each invention can be shown to have formed a separate subject for inventive effort when the examiner can show recognition of separate inventive effort by inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate status in the art may be shown by citing patents which are evidence of such separate status and also of a separate field of search. The examiner should point to facts showing independent/distinct status rather than merely stating the conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different field of search
rubrics_metrics.description: A different field of search is shown where it is necessary to search for one of the inventions in a manner that is not likely to result in finding art pertinent to the other invention(s) (e.g., searching different classes/subclasses or electronic resources, or employing different search queries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The indicated different field of search must in fact be pertinent to the subject matter covered by the claims. Patents need not be cited to show different fields of search. Examples include needing different search queries or resources for separate claimed groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking claims / rejoinder practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Linking claims are claims which, if allowable, would require rejoinder of otherwise divisible inventions (e.g., genus claims linking species claims; subcombination claims linking plural combinations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linking claims must be examined with and are considered part of the elected invention. If an allowable linking claim exists, the restriction requirement between linked inventions must be withdrawn and any nonelected claims that depend from or require all the limitations of the allowable linking claim must be rejoined and fully examined. Canceled nonelected claims may be reinstated by amendment upon allowance of the linking claim; examiners must notify applicant of this right. Be mindful of provisional double-patenting issues for continuation/divisional claims and use the appropriate form paragraphs (see MPEP § 821.04 and form ¶ 8.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of species — examiner content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where restriction between species is appropriate the examiner should send a letter including only a restriction requirement or place a telephone requirement to restrict; identify generic claims or indicate none; clearly identify each (preferably exemplary) disclosed species to which claims are to be restricted; provide reasons why the species are independent or distinct; require applicant to elect a single disclosed species under 35 U.S.C. 121 and advise as to requisites of a complete reply and rights under 37 CFR 1.141.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Species are preferably identified by figures or examples; if not, state mechanical means, particular material, or other distinguishing characteristic. If species cannot be conveniently identified, group claims by species. Form paragraphs 8.01/8.02 and related templates should be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply content and completeness to a restriction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to a restriction requirement should include a proper election along with a listing of all claims readable thereon, including any claims subsequently added. An argument that a claim is allowable or that all claims are generic is considered non-responsive unless accompanied by an election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete reply must distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the examiner’s action and reply to every ground of objection and rejection per 37 CFR 1.111(b); replies must appear to be bona fide attempts to advance the application. If the reply fails to point out errors, the election will be treated as without traverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action on the merits in restriction practice
rubrics_metrics.description: When only a nonfinal written restriction requirement is made, normally no action on the merits is given. A 1‑month (not less than 30 days) shortened statutory period is set for reply when a written restriction requirement is made without an action on the merits. The Office action making the restriction requirement final ordinarily includes an action on the merits of the claims of the elected invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When restriction/election is done by telephone and oral election made, the written record will be accompanied by a complete action on the merits of the elected claims. See rules for final actions and Ex parte Quayle practice for formal matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for making restriction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.142(a) indicates that a restriction requirement 'will normally be made before any action upon the merits; however, it may be made at any time before final action.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should make a proper requirement as early as possible in prosecution (first action if possible). Before making a restriction after a first action on the merits, the examiner should consider whether there will be a serious burden if restriction is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent/new restriction requirements and repetition after withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: A second restriction requirement may be made when it becomes proper even though there was a prior requirement with which applicant complied. Where a requirement to restrict is made and thereafter withdrawn as improper, if restriction becomes proper later in prosecution restriction may again be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior compliance or earlier withdrawal does not bar a later proper restriction; examiners should follow authority (e.g., Ex parte Benke) and make new requirements as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who should make the restriction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement should be made by an examiner who would examine at least one of the inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner should not require restriction if none of the claimed inventions is classifiable in his or her Technology Center; such applications should be transferred to a Technology Center wherein at least one claimed invention would be examined. Consult other art units if doubt exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone restriction practice procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner determines restriction should be made, the examiner should formulate a draft, telephone the attorney or agent of record and request an oral election, with or without traverse, after the attorney/agent has had time to consider the restriction requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No telephone communication needed where requirement is complex, pro se applicant, or examiner knows telephone election won't be made. Arrange a second call generally within 3 working days. If attorney objects or fails to respond, mail a restriction letter referencing the unsuccessful call. When an oral election is made, incorporate into Office action a formal restriction requirement including the date of election, attorney/agent name, and a complete record of the telephone interview, followed by a complete action on the merits of the elected invention. Use form paragraphs (e.g., 8.23, 8.23.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate exactly how the application is to be restricted — clear demarcation
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must provide a clear and detailed record of the restriction requirement to provide a clear demarcation between restricted inventions so that it can be determined whether inventions claimed in a continuing application are consonant with the restriction requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention the particular claim limitations and the reasons why such limitations support restricting claims to a particular disclosed species. Read all claims to determine what each covers and note the invention to which they are drawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping of claims and required content of restriction letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate inventions should be identified by grouping the claims with a short description of the total extent of the invention claimed in each group, specifying type/relationship (e.g., process, subcombination, product) and indicating classification or separate status (e.g., class and subclass).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline to follow: (A) Statement of requirement under 35 U.S.C. 121 (identify groups; list claims; give short description; classify each group), (B) Take into account claims not grouped and indicate disposition (linking claims, other ungrouped claims), (C) Allegation of independence or distinctness with points/facts showing independence, (D) Provide reasons for insisting upon restriction, (E) Summary statement (summarize independence and reasons; advise as to reply required; indicate effects of allowance/cancellation of linking/product claims). Use form paragraphs 8.08–8.11 and 8.14–8.20.02 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable reasons for insisting upon restriction (enumerated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable reasons to insist upon restriction include: (1) Separate status in the art; (2) Different classification; (3) Same classification but recognition of divergent subject matter; (4) Divergent fields of search; (5) Search required for one group not required for the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When alleging independence/distinctness, point out facts demonstrating independence (e.g., subcombination usable alone or in other combination; combination does not require subcombination; process/apparatus relationships; product/process of making relationships) and demonstrate by examiner’s suggestion where appropriate. Conclude restriction requirement with one of the standard form paragraphs (8.21.01–8.21.03) explaining which reason applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election and traverse procedural rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A traverse is a statement of reasons applicant relies on to conclude the restriction requirement is in error and must be complete; a provisional election must be made even when the requirement is traversed. To preserve petition rights, election must be made with traverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 37 CFR 1.111(b) and 1.143, traverse must 'distinctly and specifically point out the supposed errors' and 'reply to every ground of objection and rejection.' A mere broad allegation that the requirement is in error is insufficient and will convert the election into an election without traverse. Petition rights under 37 CFR 1.144 are preserved only if traverse is properly made; petitions must be timely filed as specified.
